(i) **Line $PQ$ situated in V.P. and inclined to H.P.:**
- Since line $PQ$ lies in the V.P., its front view (FV) coincides with its true length and inclination. 
- **Front View:** Draw a line of $70\text{ mm}$ inclined at $30^\circ$ to the $XY$ line, starting from a point $25\text{ mm}$ above $XY$ (since end $P$ is $25\text{ mm}$ above H.P.).
- **Top View (TV):** Since the line lies in the V.P., its top view lies entirely on the $XY$ reference line. Project the end points from the FV vertically down to the $XY$ line to get the top view segment.

(ii) **Line with Top View measuring $60\text{ mm}$:**
- **Top View:** Draw a horizontal line of length $60\text{ mm}$ parallel to the $XY$ line at a distance of $25\text{ mm}$ below $XY$ (since it is $25\text{ mm}$ in front of V.P. and parallel to V.P.).
- **True Length ($	ext{TL}$) Determination:** 
Let the top view be $ab = 60\text{ mm}$ and inclination to H.P. be $\theta = 45^\circ$. The true length relationship with the top view length is given by:
$$\text{Top View} = \text{True Length} \times \cos(\theta)$|
$$60 = \text{TL} \times \cos(45^\circ) \implies \text{TL} = \frac{60}{\cos(45^\circ)} = 60 \sqrt{2} \approx 84.85\text{ mm}$$
- **Front View:** Since one end lies on the H.P., draw the front view starting from the $XY$ line at an angle equal to the true inclination or construct it using the resolved components.
proTip: Remember that a line parallel to V.P. has its top view length equal to its true length only if it is also parallel to H.P. When inclined to H.P., the top view length is the true length multiplied by $\cos(\theta)$.
